claims.claim: Merck and Moderna announced the Phase 3 trial results on 19 August.
The Phase 3 trial enrolled 1,137 patients in a double-blind design.

claims.figure: 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death
claims.claim: The 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death comes from an earlier open-label trial, not the Phase 3 announcement.

claims.figure: 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death
claims.claim: The 59% reduction in the hazard of distant metastasis or death comes from an earlier open-label trial, not the Phase 3 announcement.
The earlier open-label trial enrolled 157 patients and first reported in 2023.
The earlier open-label trial of 157 patients first reported in 2023.

claims.figure: fourteen deaths — seven in each arm
claims.claim: Five-year overall survival in the earlier trial rests on fourteen deaths, seven in each arm.
The hazard ratio for overall survival in the earlier trial is 0.471.
The confidence interval around the overall survival hazard ratio in the earlier trial runs from 0.165 to 1.345.
In the earlier trial, the recurrence-free survival rate at five years was 68.8% in the treatment arm versus 49.1% in the comparison arm.
The absolute difference in five-year recurrence-free survival between arms in the earlier trial is approximately twenty percentage points.
The earlier open-label trial enrolled patients with stage IIIB–IV melanoma.
The Phase 3 trial reaches down into stage IIB melanoma.
The Phase 3 announcement reports no numerical results, including no hazard ratio, no interval, and no percentage.

Practical Dermatology, Dermatology Times, Pharmacy Times, OncoDaily and Targeted Oncology all said plainly that no Phase 3 efficacy numbers had been released and traced the 49% and 59% figures to the earlier trial.
None of the specialist trade outlets explained why figures from a smaller, unblinded trial cannot be read as the size of the new trial's effect.
The information about the earlier trial enrolling stage IIIB–IV while the Phase 3 reaches into stage IIB reached almost nobody in the coverage.
The publication acknowledges corrections within 48 hours.

studies.name: Phase 3 INTerpath-001 (NCT05933577)
studies.draft_uses: 19 August 2026 topline press release: trial met both prespecified endpoints (RFS and DMFS) in 1,137 patients; no hazard ratio or numerical data released
studies.latest_known: Same topline press release, 19 August 2026. No numerical data (hazard ratios, confidence intervals, Kaplan-Meier curves) had been publicly released as of 24 August 2026; full data presentation at an upcoming international oncology conference is pending.
studies.what_changed: Nothing changed — the draft correctly characterises the press release as containing no numerical results. The draft's description of this readout is accurate and current.

studies.name: Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 (NCT03897881) — RFS and DMFS endpoints
studies.draft_uses: The draft attributes the 49% RFS hazard reduction (HR 0.51 implied) and 59% DMFS hazard reduction to a '2023' open-label trial of 157 patients, implying it is relying on the primary analysis (~2-year follow-up, reported December 2022 / published Lancet January 2024) or the 3-year update (ASCO 2024 / JCO Oncology Advances 2026).
studies.latest_known: 5-year follow-up data (data cutoff 15 December 2025, median follow-up 60.3 months) presented at the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting on 1 June 2026 and simultaneously published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology (Abstract 9500). RFS HR = 0.510 (95% CI 0.294–0.887); DMFS HR = 0.411 (95% CI 0.200–0.843). 5-year RFS rates: 68.8% (combination) vs 49.1% (pembrolizumab alone).
studies.what_changed: The draft describes the 49%/59% figures as coming from a study that 'first reported in 2023,' implying the primary or early-update readout. In fact, those exact percentage reductions (49% RFS, 59% DMFS) now belong to the 5-year update (June 2026), not the 2023 primary analysis. The primary analysis reported a 44% RFS reduction (HR ~0.56); the 3-year update reported an updated HR. The 49% and 59% figures the draft cites are from the 5-year readout, not from 2023. The draft therefore misattributes the vintage of these specific numbers — they are more recent (and more mature) than the draft states. The 5-year RFS rates (68.8% vs 49.1%) cited in the draft are also from this 5-year update, confirming the draft is actually using the latest RFS/DMFS data but incorrectly labelling it as a '2023' result.

studies.name: Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 — Overall Survival (exploratory)
studies.draft_uses: Five-year overall survival resting on 14 deaths (7 per arm); OS HR = 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345). The draft presents this as the current state of the OS data.
studies.latest_known: The 5-year update presented at ASCO on 1 June 2026 (JCO, Abstract 9500; data cutoff 15 December 2025) reports the same OS HR of 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345) as an exploratory analysis, with 7 deaths in each arm (14 total). The 5-year OS rates were 92.2% (combination) vs 71.3% (pembrolizumab alone). This is the most recent readout of OS from KEYNOTE-942.
studies.what_changed: The OS figures the draft cites (HR 0.471, CI 0.165–1.345, 14 deaths, 7 per arm) are confirmed as the figures from the 5-year update — the most recent available readout. No newer OS data have superseded them. The draft's OS numbers are accurate and current.

objections.objection: The draft misattributes the 49% and 59% figures to the trial's 2023 first report, when they in fact come from the five-year update presented at ASCO in June 2026.
objections.quote: an open-label trial of 157 patients that first reported in 2023
objections.why: The original 2023 KEYNOTE-942 report showed a 44% RFS reduction (HR 0.561). The 49% and 59% figures cited in August 2026 coverage are from the five-year update of the same trial, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology and presented at ASCO on 1 June 2026. Describing the source of these figures as a study that 'first reported in 2023' implies the numbers are three-year-old data from a smaller snapshot, when they are in fact the most mature read of the same trial, with a median follow-up of 60.3 months. This mischaracterises the provenance and maturity of the evidence being critiqued.
objections.fix: Change to 'an open-label trial of 157 patients whose five-year update was presented at ASCO in June 2026 (the trial first reported in 2023 with a different, smaller effect estimate).'

objections.objection: The draft omits the five-year overall survival rates (92.2% vs 71.3%) while criticising others for selective reporting, making its own presentation of the OS data one-sided.
objections.quote: five-year overall survival rests on fourteen deaths — seven in each arm. Fourteen deaths. The hazard ratio is 0.471, and the interval around it runs from 0.165 to 1.345
objections.why: The draft correctly notes the wide confidence interval on the OS hazard ratio, but does not report the underlying absolute OS rates: 92.2% in the combination arm versus 71.3% in the pembrolizumab-alone arm at five years. These rates are publicly available from the same data source. Presenting only the HR and its interval — without the absolute rates that generated it — is the same selective framing the draft accuses others of. A reader is left with the impression that the OS data are essentially uninformative noise, when the point estimate and absolute rates together tell a more nuanced story. The draft's own standard requires both.
objections.fix: Add the absolute OS rates immediately after the hazard ratio: 'The underlying rates are 92.2% versus 71.3% at five years — a large absolute gap that the interval cannot yet confirm is real.'

objections.objection: The claim that 'none of them' (the listed trade publications) explained what follows from the Phase 2 limitations is an unsupported behavioural assertion about five named outlets.
objections.quote: What none of them did was explain what follows from that.
objections.why: 'None of them' is a strong, falsifiable claim about the editorial choices of five named publications. If any one of them included even a partial explanation of why Phase 2 figures cannot be read as the Phase 3 effect size, the sentence is wrong and those outlets could reasonably object. The draft provides no quotation or link to demonstrate the absence. Absence of evidence in a brief scan is not the same as evidence of absence across all coverage by all five outlets.
objections.fix: Qualify to 'None of the coverage reviewed for this piece explained what follows from that' and link to or list the specific articles reviewed, so the claim is bounded and checkable.

objections.objection: Describing the Phase 2b trial as 'a different study' without noting it is the direct predecessor trial cited by the companies themselves in the Phase 3 announcement frames a normal evidentiary relationship as a suspicious sleight of hand.
objections.quote: The figures in the headlines...come from a different study
objections.why: KEYNOTE-942 is not an unrelated study that figures were borrowed from opportunistically. It is the Phase 2b trial that motivated the Phase 3, was cited by Merck and Moderna in their own announcement, and whose five-year data were presented at ASCO two months before the Phase 3 readout. Referring to it only as 'a different study' implies the companies or journalists were substituting unrelated data, when referencing the predecessor Phase 2b trial in a Phase 3 topline announcement — before Phase 3 data are released — is standard practice in oncology communications.
objections.fix: Change to 'the predecessor Phase 2b trial' or 'the earlier Phase 2b study that motivated the Phase 3,' so readers understand the relationship rather than inferring deception.

inferences.quote: the figures in the headlines, a 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death and 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death, come from a different study: an open-label trial of 157 patients that first reported in 2023
inferences.problem: The 49% (HR 0.51) and 59% (HR 0.411) figures are from the five-year update of KEYNOTE-942 presented at ASCO in June 2026, not from the original 2023 report; the 2023 report showed a 44% RFS reduction (HR 0.561) and a 65% DMFS reduction (HR 0.347) — materially different numbers attributed to the wrong time-point.
inferences.correct_reading: The 49% and 59% figures come from the five-year follow-up of KEYNOTE-942, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology and presented at ASCO 2026; the trial's original 2023 report showed different effect estimates (HR 0.561 for RFS, HR 0.347 for DMFS).
inferences.fix: the figures in the headlines, a 49% reduction in the hazard of recurrence or death and 59% in the hazard of distant metastasis or death, come from a different study: an open-label trial of 157 patients whose five-year follow-up was presented at ASCO in June 2026 (the same trial first reported smaller, different estimates in 2023)

inferences.quote: the interval around it runs from 0.165 to 1.345 — from a rate of death about a sixth of the comparison group's, to about 35% higher
inferences.problem: A confidence interval bound is not a rate: 0.165 is the lower limit of the uncertainty range for the hazard ratio, not an estimate of the death rate in either arm; converting CI bounds into counts or rates is the exact error the draft elsewhere warns against.
inferences.correct_reading: The 95% confidence interval runs from HR 0.165 to HR 1.345, meaning the data are compatible with anything from a very large reduction in the hazard of death to a 35% increase; neither bound is a rate, and neither should be read as a point estimate of effect.
inferences.fix: the interval around it runs from 0.165 to 1.345 — meaning the data are consistent with anything from a very large reduction in the hazard of death to a hazard about 35% higher than the comparison group's; the interval is too wide to exclude either a substantial benefit or a small harm

inferences.quote: five-year overall survival rests on fourteen deaths — seven in each arm
inferences.problem: The draft presents the OS analysis without noting that overall survival was a pre-specified exploratory endpoint in KEYNOTE-942, not a powered or confirmatory one; a reader may infer this is an underpowered confirmatory analysis rather than an analysis that was never designed to be conclusive.
inferences.correct_reading: Overall survival was a pre-specified exploratory endpoint in KEYNOTE-942, so the wide interval reflects both the small number of events and the fact that the trial was never powered to detect an OS difference; the HR and CI describe a signal, not a test.
inferences.fix: five-year overall survival — an exploratory endpoint the trial was not powered to assess — rests on fourteen deaths, seven in each arm

inferences.quote: It says the trial met both prespecified endpoints — a real finding, from 1,137 patients in a double-blind trial — and gives no hazard ratio, no interval, no percentage.
inferences.problem: The sentence is sound on its own, but the immediately preceding sentence says 'The announcement reports no numerical results,' which a reader will quote in isolation; meeting prespecified endpoints is itself a numerical result (a binary outcome of a statistical test), so 'no numerical results' misstates what the announcement contains — the missing thing is magnitude, not evidence of effect.
inferences.correct_reading: The announcement reports that both endpoints were met with statistical significance — which is a result — but reports no effect sizes: no hazard ratio, no confidence interval, no absolute rates.
inferences.fix: The announcement reports that both prespecified endpoints were met — a result — but gives no effect sizes: no hazard ratio, no confidence interval, no percentage.

contradictions.quote: The specialist trade press largely got this right. Practical Dermatology, Dermatology Times, Pharmacy Times, OncoDaily and Targeted Oncology all said plainly that no Phase 3 efficacy numbers had been released, and traced the 49% and 59% to the earlier trial.
contradictions.counterexample: This claim is broadly supported. All five named outlets did correctly attribute the 49%/59% figures to the Phase 2b KEYNOTE-942 trial and noted no Phase 3 efficacy numbers had been released. The ASCO Post, Biotech Blueprint, Morning Glory Sciences, and BioPharma Dive also got this right, so the correct-attribution group is larger than the draft implies.
contradictions.fix: Expand the list of outlets that got attribution right; the failure was not universal even in general trade and specialist press.

contradictions.quote: What none of them did was explain what follows from that. Why figures from a smaller, unblinded trial cannot be read as the size of the new one's effect.
contradictions.counterexample: OncoDaily explicitly stated the result 'should be described precisely as a positive Phase 3 topline readout, rather than as evidence of a defined magnitude of survival benefit,' and called for the full dataset to determine 'the magnitude of the RFS and DMFS improvements.' This is a direct statement of why Phase 2b figures cannot be read as the Phase 3 effect size.
contradictions.fix: Narrow the claim: most outlets did not explain this, but OncoDaily came close. Reframe as 'almost none of them explained…' or 'only OncoDaily gestured at this, without spelling out the mechanism.'

contradictions.quote: What none of them did was explain what follows from that… What fourteen deaths can and cannot establish.
contradictions.counterexample: Oncology Central reported that 'seven patients in each treatment group died during follow-up' — directly naming the fourteen-death basis for the OS analysis, though without discussing what that event count implies for the confidence interval.
contradictions.fix: The claim that no outlet named the fourteen deaths is false; Oncology Central did. The stronger and still-accurate claim is that no outlet explained what fourteen deaths implies for the width of the confidence interval or the reliability of the OS estimate.

contradictions.quote: And one thing that reached almost nobody: the earlier trial enrolled stage IIIB–IV, while the Phase 3 reaches down into stage IIB.
contradictions.counterexample: Morning Glory Sciences explicitly noted that 'the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV; the Phase 3 adds stage IIB and IIC — node-negative disease' and that 'absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit.' Targeted Oncology also correctly identified the Phase 2b population as 'stage IIIB to IV' while noting the Phase 3 enrolled stage IIB–IV.
contradictions.fix: Change 'reached almost nobody' to 'reached very few outlets.' Morning Glory Sciences stated it explicitly and drew the correct implication about absolute benefit. The draft can legitimately add that this point was absent from the major specialist trade outlets (Dermatology Times, Pharmacy Times, OncoDaily, Targeted Oncology, Practical Dermatology) but should not claim it reached nobody.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet found — including the most careful ones — reported the OS hazard ratio (0.471) alongside its confidence interval (0.165–1.345) and explained that this interval, spanning from roughly one-sixth the comparison group's death rate to 35% higher, is too wide to distinguish a large survival benefit from a small harm; that gap between the headline OS signal and what the data can actually establish is the layer the draft uniquely supplies. The draft can also add the explicit arithmetic: fourteen total deaths (seven per arm) is the event count driving that interval, and no outlet connected those three facts — the death count, the interval width, and what that means for reading the OS trend — in a single place.
